 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.12,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 10.4.2018 at about 1.30 p.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 proceeding on Hosahalli road, Doddagollarahatti,
Bengaluru at that time, the rider of the said motor cycle rode the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and suddenly applied the break and jumped the path holes.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately she was shifted to Shri Krishna hospital, Gollarahatti, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident she was hale and healthy,
aged about 35 years, doing tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statements.

The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, placed exparte.
5.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 and its validity.
Further denied the manner of the accident, involvement of the vehicle.
Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against it with cost.
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 on 1.4.2018 about 1.30 p.m. near Hosahalli Road,

My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:

R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:-
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved her case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent has argued that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 has not at all involved in the accident and prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondents.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and she has stated in her evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of her evidence, she has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P1 to ExP5 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
15. On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by petitioner on 10.4.2018.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Byadarahalli Police in Cr.
No.252/2018 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA- 02-JK-4549 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar reveals that the alleged incident was taken place and it corroborates the version of PW1.
On perusal of Ex.
P3 - IMV report also reveals that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.
The counsel for the respondent No.1 has argued that the vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
To substantiate the said fact the respondent No.1 has not led any rebuttal evidence in order to prove its defence.
On the other hand the petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that she met with an accident on 10.4.2018 at about 1.30 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to Shri Krishna Hospital,
Gollarahatti, Bengaluru.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P4, which discloses the following injuries;
1)Dislocation of left shoulder 2)Fracture greater tuberosity left humerus 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which shows that she was admitted on 10.4.2018 and discharged on 16.4.2018 and underwent reduction.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor.

21. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
22.
The case of the petitioner is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 35 years, doing tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
She has produced the certificates for taken the tailoring course, which are marked at Ex.P10 to Ex.P12.
She has not produced any documents pertains to her income from tailoring.
In the absence of the same it is very difficult to believe the income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner, if Rs.8,500/- per month is considered it will meet the ends of justice.
So, considering the nature of the injuries she might have taken rest and treatment atleast for two months.
Therefore, two months income comes to Rs.17,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.

The contention of the petitioner is that, she has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
On record she has produced the medical bills at Ex.P7 to the extent of Rs.44,226/- supported with prescriptions.
So, considering the evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.44,226/- under the head of medical expenses.
24. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 35 years.
Due to severe injuries she is permanently disabled.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability.
Therefore no amount is granted under this head.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
So her happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out her life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.5,000/- under the head of amenities.
26. PW1 has stated in her evidence that due to the accident she took the treatment as inpatient and also as outpatient.
On perusal of discharge summary at Ex.P6, it appears that, the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 10.4.2018 to 16.4.2018.
Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, so, one must attend her for the period of hospitalization and rest period.

Therefore, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
27.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs. 40,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 17,000-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 44,226-00 4. Loss of future earning Nil 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 5,000-00 6.
Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 15,000-00 conveyance charges Rs.1,21,226-00 28.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549.
29.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation.

30. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of IMV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,226/- with interest @8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest at 8%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized/scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
